claim: The PNG kinase complex regulates maternal mRNA translation at the oocyte-to-embryo transition in Drosophila.
source: In Drosophila, the PNG kinase complex is a master regulator of mRNA translation at the oocyte-to-embryo transition.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Lee et al., 2003; Tadros et al., 2007; Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007; Kronja et al., 2014a) and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: The GNU activating subunit is crucial in regulating PNG and timing its activity to the window between egg activation and early embryogenesis.
source: We previously showed that the GNU activating subunit is crucial in regulating PNG and timing its activity to the window between egg activation and early embryogenesis (Hara et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hara et al., 2017.

claim: GNU localizes to cytoplasmic RNP granules in the mature oocyte.
source: In this study, we find associations between GNU and proteins of RNP granules and demonstrate that GNU localizes to cytoplasmic RNP granules in the mature oocyte, identifying GNU as a new component of a subset of RNP granules.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data including immunoprecipitation and localization studies described in the Results section.

claim: GNU binds to BIC-C to localize to RNP granules.
source: Interactions between GNU and the granule component BIC-C reveal potential conserved functions for translational regulation in metazoan development.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, and localization studies presented in the Results section.

claim: Upon egg activation, GNU brings PNG to its initial targets, translational repressors in RNP granules.
source: We propose that by binding to BIC-C, upon egg activation GNU brings PNG to its initial targets, translational repressors in RNP granules.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on inference from the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: Around 90% of all transcripts present in the activated egg are completely or partially dependent on PNG to either activate or inhibit their translation following egg activation.
source: Initially shown to control translation of a few targets (cyclins A and B, smg) (Tadros et al., 2007; Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007), recent analyses of global translation revealed that around 90% of all transcripts present in the activated egg are completely or partially dependent on PNG to either activate or inhibit their translation following egg activation (Kronja et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kronja et al., 2014a.

claim: PNG phosphorylates the translational regulators TRAL, ME31B, and BIC-C following egg activation.
source: Following egg activation, PNG phosphorylates the translational regulators TRAL, ME31B, and BIC-C amongst other regulators of mRNA translation (Hara et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hara et al., 2018.

claim: Phosphorylation of GNU by CDK1/CYCB inhibits its binding to the PNG complex in mature oocytes.
source: Whereas PNG and PLU are bound in mature oocytes, phosphorylation of GNU by CDK1/CYCB inhibits its binding to the complex (Hara et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hara et al., 2017.

claim: Upon egg activation, GNU is dephosphorylated and is then able to bind and activate the kinase activity of the PNG complex.
source: Upon egg activation, GNU is dephosphorylated, and it is then able to bind and activate the kinase activity of the complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Hara et al., 2017) and represents established knowledge.

claim: The PNG complex is inactivated following egg activation by PNG-dependent degradation of GNU.
source: The complex is once again inactivated following egg activation by PNG-dependent degradation of GNU, thereby limiting its activity to the oocyte-to-embryo transition.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Hara et al., 2017).

claim: Egg activation triggers the disassembly of oocyte RNP granules in Drosophila.
source: In Drosophila, egg activation triggers the disassembly of these 'oocyte' granules (Weil et al., 2012), and they reform as 'embryonic' RNP complexes in early embryos (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Weil et al., 2012 and Wang et al., 2017.

claim: BIC-C was the most enriched protein recovered in GNU-GFP immunoprecipitations from mature oocytes.
source: The translational repressor BIC-C had the most enriched interaction with GNU (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry analysis following immunoprecipitation, as shown in Table 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The interaction between GNU and BIC-C does not depend on RNA.
source: Furthermore, the interaction with BIC-C was not affected by the treatment of extracts with RNase A, indicating that this interaction does not depend on RNA (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that RNase A treatment did not affect the interaction, as shown in Table 1.

claim: Components of the PP2A phosphatase complex (MTS, PP2A-29B, and TWS) were highly enriched in GNU-GFP pull-downs.
source: Another major group of proteins isolated after immunoprecipitation were components of the PP2A phosphatase complex, MTS, PP2A-29B, and TWS. These proteins were highly enriched in GNU-GFP pull-downs over no GFP control (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry analysis, as shown in Table 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The interaction of GNU with BIC-C depends on the CDK1 phosphorylation state of GNU.
source: However, BIC-C was significantly lower in GNU9A-GFP than in GNUWT-GFP precipitates, suggesting that the interaction of GNU with BIC-C depends on the CDK1 phosphorylation state of GNU.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry comparing GNU9A-GFP and GNUWT-GFP.

claim: The SAM domain of GNU is necessary for the interaction with BIC-C.
source: We found that most interactions were unaffected by deletion of the SAM domain, with only the interaction of GNU with BIC-C being blocked (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry and immunoblot analysis, as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and Figure 1A.

claim: GNU directly interacts with BIC-C in vitro.
source: We observed that MBP-GNU was pulled down with GST-BIC-C (Figure 2A). Moreover, deleting the SAM domain of GNU resulted in only background levels of GNU in eluates following GST-BIC-C pull-down (Figure 2A). Our in vitro experiments support the in vivo results of the requirement of the SAM domain of GNU for BIC-C association and indicate that GNU directly interacts with BIC-C.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vitro pull-down assays, as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The gnuΔSAM-gfp transgene confers only partial rescue of the gnu null phenotype.
source: We observed only partial rescue of the gnu phenotype in embryos laid by gnuΔSAM-gfp females (Figure 2B,C). In contrast, most gnuwt-gfp developed normally (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from phenotypic analysis of embryos, as shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: CYCB is present in early embryos from gnuΔSAM-gfp females, though at lower levels than in gnuwt-gfp control embryos.
source: We found that CYCB was present in early embryos from gnuΔSAM-gfp females, though at lower levels than in gnuwt-gfp control embryos (Figure 2D, compare lanes 8 and 9 to 10 and 11).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunoblot analysis, as shown in Figure 2D.

claim: GNUΔSAM can activate PNG kinase in vitro at levels comparable to GNUWT.
source: We found that incubation with MBP-GNUΔSAM resulted in PNG kinase activity comparable to incubation with MBP-GNUWT (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vitro kinase assays, as shown in Figure 2E.

claim: BIC-C protein levels are decreased in embryos from gnuΔSAM-gfp lines compared to embryos from gnuwt-gfp.
source: However, we saw decreased BIC-C levels in embryos from both gnuΔSAM-gfp lines compared to embryos from gnuwt-gfp (Figure 2D, compare lanes 8 and 9 to 10 and 11).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunoblot analysis, as shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The SAM domain of GNU is necessary for its degradation following egg activation.
source: The persistence of GNU protein in the gnuΔSAM-gfp transgene lines suggests that the SAM domain of GNU is necessary for its degradation following egg activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GNU levels remain high in gnuΔSAM-gfp embryos compared to wild-type and gnuwt-gfp embryos.

claim: GNU-GFP localizes to granular cytoplasmic structures in mature oocytes.
source: We found that GNU-GFP localized to granular cytoplasmic structures in mature oocytes (Figure 3B, top row), whereas no such structures were observed in the absence of a gnu-gfp transgene (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: GNUWT-GFP signal becomes dispersed through the cytoplasm in in vitro activated eggs.
source: We found that GNUWT-GFP signal became dispersed through the cytoplasm in in vitro activated eggs from both gnuwt-gfp transgenic lines (Figure 3B, bottom row), consistent with GNU granules dissociating upon egg activation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy of in vitro activated eggs, as shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The dispersal of GNU following egg activation is not dependent on PNG function.
source: The dispersal of GNU following egg activation is not dependent on PNG function, as we did not observe a difference in localization of GNUWT-GFP in png mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy in png mutants, as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PNG and PLU do not exhibit a granular localization in mature oocytes.
source: Interestingly, PNG and PLU do not exhibit a granular localization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: GNUWT-mKATE2 co-localizes with both TRAL-GFP and ME31B-GFP in cytoplasmic granules.
source: We found that GNUWT-mKATE2 co-localized with both TRAL-GFP and ME31B-GFP in cytoplasmic granules (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 4.

claim: Most GNUWT-mKATE2 co-localizes with TRAL-GFP and ME31B-GFP, but only a fraction of all observed TRAL-GFP and ME31B-GFP granules also contain GNUWT-mKATE2.
source: Whereas most GNUWT-mKATE2 co-localized with TRAL-GFP and ME31B-GFP, only a fraction of all observed TRAL-GFP and ME31B-GFP granules also contained GNUWT-mKATE2 (Figure 4A', B').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 4A' and 4B'.

claim: GNU-containing granules represent a subpopulation of TRAL- and ME31B-containing RNP granules present in mature oocytes.
source: These observations are consistent with GNU localizing to RNP granules, with GNU-containing granules representing a subpopulation of TRAL- and ME31B-containing RNP granules present in mature oocytes.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-localization data showing that GNU is present in only a subset of TRAL and ME31B granules.

claim: GNU9A-GFP exhibits mostly dispersed localization in the oocyte cytoplasm with some bright cytoplasmic puncta.
source: We observed mostly dispersed localization for GNU9A-GFP in the oocyte cytoplasm, although there were some bright cytoplasmic puncta present (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 3C.

claim: CDK1 phosphorylation plays a role in modulating GNU localization to RNP granules.
source: The difference in localization of GNU9A-GFP as compared to wild type is consistent with a role for CDK1 phosphorylation in modulating GNU localization.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GNU9A-GFP, which cannot be phosphorylated by CDK1, shows altered localization compared to wild-type GNU.

claim: GNUWT-mKATE2 and BIC-C-GFP co-localize in mature oocytes.
source: GNUWT-mKATE2 and BIC-C-GFP co-localized (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Most GNU granules contain BIC-C, but GNU-containing granules represent only a fraction of all BIC-C granules.
source: Moreover, whereas most GNU granules contained BIC-C, GNU-containing granules represented only a fraction of all BIC-C granules (Figure 5A').
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 5A'.

claim: GNUΔSAM-GFP exhibits a dispersed localization in the cytoplasm of mature oocytes.
source: We found that in contrast to the granular localization observed in GNUWT-GFP, GNUΔSAM-GFP exhibited a dispersed localization in the cytoplasm of mature oocytes (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The SAM domain of GNU is required for GNU localization to RNP granules.
source: We found that in contrast to the granular localization observed in GNUWT-GFP, GNUΔSAM-GFP exhibited a dispersed localization in the cytoplasm of mature oocytes (Figure 5B), evidence that the SAM domain of GNU is required for GNU localization to RNP granules.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy showing that deletion of the SAM domain disrupts granular localization.

claim: BIC-C is required for GNU localization to RNP granules.
source: However, GNUWT-GFP localization was disrupted in Bic-C4/Bic-CPE37 mutant oocytes. GNU-GFP exhibited a mostly dispersed appearance in these oocytes, reminiscent of GNUΔSAM-GFP localization, but with a portion of GNU-GFP still localized to granules. The effect of Bic-C mutations on GNUWT-GFP localization raises the possibility that the reduced granular localization observed for GNU9A-GFP (Figure 3C) could be due in part to its weakened interaction with BIC-C (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy in Bic-C mutants, as shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Loss of gnu function results in an observable effect on BIC-C-GFP localization in 30% of mature oocytes.
source: We found that loss of gnu function resulted in an observable effect on BIC-C-GFP localization (Figure 5D), because the localization of BIC-C became partially dispersed in 30% of gnu mutant oocytes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy in gnu mutants, as shown in Figure 5D.

claim: ME31B-GFP localization is unaffected in gnu mutant oocytes.
source: To address this issue, we also examined the localization of ME31B-GFP in gnu mutant oocytes, finding no effect on ME31B-GFP in these mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy, as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: GNU retains its association with BIC-C after egg activation.
source: We repeated the immunoprecipitation experiments to test for association between GNU and BIC-C, this time comparing mature oocytes with in vitro activated eggs (Figure 6A). GNU clearly retained its association with BIC-C after egg activation, a result not readily consistent with the sequestration model.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation/immunoblot analysis, as shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Deletion of the SAM domain in GNU does not increase levels of CYCB in mature oocytes.
source: Levels of CYCB were comparable or slightly lower in gnuΔSAM-gfp oocytes than in gnuwt-gfp mature oocytes. There was a small but significant reduction of CYCB levels in gnuΔSAM-gfp3-2 mature oocytes, but not in gnuΔSAM-gfp3-8 mature oocytes, as compared to gnuwt-gfp oocytes (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunoblot analysis, as shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Loss of granule localization is not sufficient to activate PNG in mature oocytes.
source: These results are consistent with the loss of granule localization not being sufficient to activate PNG.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CYCB levels do not increase in gnuΔSAM-gfp oocytes despite loss of granule localization.

claim: GNU is a previously unidentified component of RNP granules in oocytes.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that GNU, the lynchpin to the developmentally regulated activation of PNG (Hara et al., 2017), is a previously unidentified component of RNP granules in oocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, and localization studies.

claim: GNU forms a complex with translational repressors in mature oocytes.
source: We find that GNU forms a complex with translational repressors in mature oocytes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry showing interactions with BIC-C, TYF, and YPS.

claim: GNU-containing granules represent a new subpopulation of oocyte RNP granules.
source: Because TRAL and ME31B are thought to be present in all granules (Kato and Nakamura, 2012), the present findings identify GNU-containing granules as a new subpopulation of oocyte RNP granules.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GNU is present in only a subset of TRAL and ME31B granules, combined with knowledge that TRAL and ME31B are present in all granules.

claim: BIC-C granules are present in mature Drosophila oocytes.
source: To our knowledge, this is also the first report of the presence of BIC-C granules in mature Drosophila oocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy showing BIC-C-GFP localization.

claim: GNU is recruited to RNP granules via specific protein-protein interactions through its SAM domain.
source: The observation that the SAM domain is required for the localization of GNU to granules as well as its interaction with BIC-C is consistent with a model in which GNU is recruited to RNP granules via specific protein-protein interactions through its SAM domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that the SAM domain is required for both BIC-C interaction and granule localization.

claim: GNU contains an intrinsically disordered region (IDR) that contains eight of the nine CDK1 phosphorylation sites.
source: Interestingly, in addition to the SAM domain, GNU also contains an intrinsically disordered region (IDR) that contains eight of the nine CDK1 phosphorylation sites (Hara et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hara et al., 2017.

claim: CDK1 phosphorylation of GNU may act to enhance or stabilize the interaction with RNP granules.
source: The observation that GNU9A has reduced granular localization is consistent with the idea that CDK phosphorylation may act to enhance or stabilize the interaction with RNP granules.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GNU9A, which cannot be phosphorylated by CDK1, shows reduced granular localization.

claim: The interaction between BIC-C and GNU is the main mechanism by which GNU is recruited into RNP granules.
source: Here, we identified an in vivo interaction between BIC-C and GNU in mature oocytes dependent on the SAM domain of GNU; we propose this is the main mechanism by which GNU is recruited into RNP granules.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on inference from the experimental findings showing that the SAM domain is required for BIC-C interaction and granule localization.

claim: CDK1/CYCB phosphorylation of GNU in mature oocytes aids in stabilizing GNU in RNP granules, possibly through strengthening the interaction of GNU with BIC-C.
source: It appears that CDK1/CYCB phosphorylation of GNU in mature oocytes aids in stabilizing GNU in RNP granules, possibly through strengthening the interaction of GNU with BIC-C in these structures.
evidence: This is inferred from the observations that GNU9A shows reduced interaction with BIC-C and reduced granular localization.

claim: GNU may be recruited onto pre-existing BIC-C-containing granules as its levels increase during oocyte maturation.
source: Because BIC-C-containing granules are present in oocytes starting at mid-oogenesis (Kugler et al., 2009), and GNU levels increase later during oocyte maturation (Hara et al., 2017; Kronja et al., 2014b), GNU may be recruited onto pre-existing granules as its levels increase.
evidence: This is inferred from the timing of BIC-C granule formation and GNU expression, supported by citations.

claim: GNU has a role in maintaining or stabilizing BIC-C in granules.
source: We found an effect on BIC-C localization in gnu mutant oocytes, where BIC-C granules are diminished and take on a more dispersed appearance. The affected granules are presumed to be the subpopulation of BIC-C granules that also contain higher levels of GNU. If so, this suggests that GNU has a role in maintaining or stabilizing BIC-C in granules.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BIC-C localization is disrupted in gnu mutants.

claim: The SAM domain of GNU is required for maintaining BIC-C protein levels in early embryos.
source: We also observed a requirement of the SAM domain of GNU, and likely the interaction with BIC-C, in maintaining BIC-C protein levels in early embryos, which indicates modulation of BIC-C stability by GNU.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BIC-C levels are reduced in gnuΔSAM-gfp embryos.

claim: There is a diverse pool of RNP granule subtypes in the mature oocyte.
source: An implication of our work is the presence of a diverse pool of RNP granule subtypes in the mature oocyte.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GNU is present in only a subset of TRAL, ME31B, and BIC-C granules.

claim: In the beacon model, GNU is recruited into granules as a mechanism to mark these granules to target PNG to them.
source: In this model, GNU is recruited into granules as a mechanism to mark these granules to target PNG to them. As egg activation occurs, GNU is dephosphorylated and recruits PNG to the disassembling granules, where it can phosphorylate TRAL, ME31B, BIC-C, and potentially other translation regulators.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on inference from the experimental findings, particularly the observation that GNU remains associated with BIC-C after egg activation.

claim: The data are more consistent with the beacon model than the sequestration model of PNG regulation.
source: The data are more consistent with a 'beacon' model of regulation of PNG (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings, particularly that GNU remains associated with BIC-C after egg activation and that loss of granule localization does not activate PNG.

claim: GNU may have PNG-independent roles in regulating maternal mRNA translation in mature oocytes.
source: A final implication of this work is the possible roles of GNU in addition to the activation of PNG. Whether GNU regulation of PNG follows the 'sequestration' or 'beacon' models, the presence of GNU in oocytes suggests a potential PNG-independent role in regulating maternal mRNA translation.
evidence: This is speculative, based on the observation that GNU is present in oocytes where PNG is inactive.

claim: During left-right patterning in frog and fish, BICC1 can bind to the ankyrin-repeat proteins ANKS3 and ANKS6.
source: During left-right patterning in frog and fish, BICC1, the BIC-C homolog, can bind to the ankyrin-repeat proteins ANKS3 and ANKS6 (Rothé et al., 2018; Rothé et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rothé et al., 2018 and Rothé et al., 2020.

claim: The interaction with ANKS3 can recruit a Ser/Thr kinase, NEK7, to regulate left-right patterning by restricting its activity to the right side of the animal.
source: The interaction with ANKS3 can recruit a Ser/Thr kinase, NEK7, to regulate left-right patterning by restricting its activity to the right side of the animal (Ramachandran et al., 2015; Rothé et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ramachandran et al., 2015 and Rothé et al., 2020.

claim: The model of regulation of NEK7 by ANKS3 and BICC1 is reminiscent of the model of regulation of PNG activity by GNU and BIC-C.
source: This model of regulation of NEK7 by ANKS3 and BICC1 is reminiscent of our model of regulation of PNG activity by GNU and BIC-C.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the two regulatory systems.

claim: ANKS6 and ANKS3 contain a SAM domain and can interact with BICC1 via SAM:SAM domain interactions.
source: Interestingly, in addition to the ankyrin repeats, ANKS6 and ANKS3 also contain a SAM domain, and they can interact with BICC1 via SAM:SAM domain interactions (Bakey et al., 2015; Rothé et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bakey et al., 2015 and Rothé et al., 2018.

claim: The similarities between the regulation of the PNG complex and the NEK7 complex suggest that similar control mechanisms are at play in different developmental contexts.
source: The similarities between the regulation of these two complexes suggest that similar control mechanisms are at play in different developmental contexts.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the two regulatory systems and their structural similarities.

claim: The active PNG kinase requires the PNG catalytic subunit and the PLU and GNU activating subunits.
source: The active kinase requires the PNG catalytic subunit, a kinase with a preference for threonine (Hara et al., 2018), and the PLU and GNU activating subunits (Lee et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hara et al., 2018 and Lee et al., 2003.

claim: PNG is a kinase with a preference for threonine.
source: The active kinase requires the PNG catalytic subunit, a kinase with a preference for threonine (Hara et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hara et al., 2018.

claim: Phosphorylation by PNG is thought to inhibit the translational repressor activity of TRAL and PUM.
source: Phosphorylation by PNG is thought to inhibit the translational repressor activity of TRAL and PUM (Hara et al., 2018; Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hara et al., 2018 and Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007.

claim: PNG activity is required for the degradation of ME31B and TRAL at the onset of the maternal-to-zygotic transition later in embryogenesis.
source: PNG activity also is required for the degradation of ME31B and TRAL at the onset of the maternal-to-zygotic transition (MZT) later in embryogenesis (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2017.

claim: Translation of PNG mRNA targets such as smg is required for translational repression and clearance of maternal transcripts at the MZT.
source: In addition, translation of PNG mRNA targets such as smg is required for translational repression and clearance of maternal transcripts at the MZT (Tadros et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tadros et al., 2007.

claim: PNG can affect both polyadenylation and deadenylation of maternal mRNAs.
source: PNG can affect both polyadenylation and deadenylation of maternal mRNAs (Eichhorn et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Eichhorn et al., 2016.

claim: DDX6 (Drosophila ME31B) and LSM14 (Drosophila TRAL) are key conserved protein components of P-bodies.
source: Along with the RNA components of RNP granules, conserved protein components of P-bodies have been identified (Hubstenberger et al., 2017; Standart and Weil, 2018), with DDX6 (Drosophila ME31B) and LSM14 (aka RAP55 and Drosophila TRAL) being key.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hubstenberger et al., 2017 and Standart and Weil, 2018.

claim: TRAL and ME31B are localized in RNP granules in Drosophila oocytes.
source: In Drosophila oocytes, both TRAL and ME31B are localized in RNP granules (Nakamura et al., 2001; Wilhelm et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nakamura et al., 2001 and Wilhelm et al., 2005.

claim: BIC-C localizes to RNP granules in oocytes of some species, such as in Drosophila.
source: Another translational repressor, BIC-C, also localizes to RNP granules in oocytes of some species, such as in Drosophila (Kugler et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kugler et al., 2009.

claim: BIC-C and YPS form a complex with TRAL, ME31B, and CUP during oogenesis.
source: Interestingly, BIC-C and YPS form a complex with TRAL, ME31B, and CUP during oogenesis (Chicoine et al., 2007; Kugler et al., 2009; Wilhelm et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chicoine et al., 2007, Kugler et al., 2009, and Wilhelm et al., 2005.

claim: GNU and BIC-C were found to interact in yeast two-hybrid tests.
source: GNU and BIC-C were found previously to interact in yeast two-hybrid tests (Chicoine et al., 2007; Giot et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chicoine et al., 2007 and Giot et al., 2003.

claim: The Bic-C4 allele results in no BIC-C protein.
source: The Bic-C4 allele results in no BIC-C protein, and the Bic-CPE37 allele reduces protein levels (Saffman et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Saffman et al., 1998.

claim: The Bic-CPE37 allele reduces BIC-C protein levels.
source: The Bic-C4 allele results in no BIC-C protein, and the Bic-CPE37 allele reduces protein levels (Saffman et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Saffman et al., 1998.

claim: Mutations in Bic-C that significantly reduce or abolish Bic-C function result in a dominant embryonic patterning defect.
source: Mutations in Bic-C that significantly reduce or abolish Bic-C function result in a dominant embryonic patterning defect (Schüpbach and Wieschaus, 1991)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schüpbach and Wieschaus, 1991.

claim: Mutations in Bic-C result in an arrest in early oogenesis in homozygous mutant females.
source: Mutations in Bic-C that significantly reduce or abolish Bic-C function result in a dominant embryonic patterning defect (Schüpbach and Wieschaus, 1991), as well as in an arrest in early oogenesis in homozygous mutant females (Mahone et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mahone et al., 1995.

claim: Null mutations in gnu result in a characteristic giant nuclei phenotype in embryos due to DNA replication without nuclear division.
source: Null mutations in gnu result in a characteristic giant nuclei phenotype in embryos due to DNA replication without nuclear division (Freeman and Glover, 1987).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Freeman and Glover, 1987.

claim: The giant nuclei phenotype observed in gnu mutants is due to a lack of cycB translation.
source: The giant nuclei phenotype observed in gnu mutants is due to a lack of cycB translation, which results in DNA replication without nuclear division (Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007.

claim: Translation of cycB mRNA upon egg activation is completely dependent on PNG.
source: Translation of cycB mRNA upon egg activation is completely dependent on PNG (Kronja et al., 2014a; Lee et al., 2001; Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kronja et al., 2014a, Lee et al., 2001, and Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007.

claim: PNG function is not required for translation of Bic-C mRNA in oocytes or following egg activation.
source: Previous work demonstrated that PNG function is not required for translation of Bic-C mRNA in oocytes or following egg activation (Kronja et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kronja et al., 2014a.

claim: In png mutant-activated eggs, BIC-C protein levels were reduced relative to wild type.
source: Consistent with PNG kinase activity being important, quantitative proteomic studies showed that in png mutant-activated eggs BIC-C protein levels were reduced relative to wild type (Kronja et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kronja et al., 2014b.

claim: GNU is degraded in early embryos by a PNG-dependent mechanism.
source: GNU is degraded in early embryos by a PNG-dependent mechanism (Hara et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hara et al., 2017.

claim: SAM domains can mediate both protein-protein and protein-RNA interactions.
source: SAM domains can mediate both protein-protein and protein-RNA interactions (Green et al., 2003; Kim and Bowie, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Green et al., 2003 and Kim and Bowie, 2003.

claim: Intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), although alone not sufficient for granule localization, can form weak non-specific interactions that stabilize their localization within RNP granules.
source: Studies on RNP granule assembly have suggested that IDRs, although alone not sufficient for granule localization, can form weak non-specific interactions that stabilize their localization within RNP granules (Lin et al., 2015; Protter et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lin et al., 2015 and Protter et al., 2018.

claim: In mammalian axons, phosphorylation of FMRP promotes assembly of FMRP granules.
source: For example, in mammalian axons, phosphorylation of FMRP promotes assembly of FMRP granules, and in response to action potentials, dephosphorylation of FMRP promotes their disassembly (Tsang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tsang et al., 2019.

claim: In Caenorhabditis elegans, phosphorylation of the MEG granule proteins promotes granule disassembly.
source: The opposite effect of phosphorylation can occur; in Caenorhabditis elegans phosphorylation of the MEG granule proteins promotes granule disassembly (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2014.

claim: BIC-C-containing granules are present in oocytes starting at mid-oogenesis.
source: Because BIC-C-containing granules are present in oocytes starting at mid-oogenesis (Kugler et al., 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kugler et al., 2009.

claim: GNU levels increase during oocyte maturation.
source: GNU levels increase later during oocyte maturation (Hara et al., 2017; Kronja et al., 2014b)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hara et al., 2017 and Kronja et al., 2014b.
